why: Both correct (63/47/24%), but A puts the 2.6x insight in a subtitle and accents only first class, while B buries the insight in a footnote and leaves a wide empty right margin.
A keeps cylinder count in its natural ordinal order and highlights the 8-cylinder bar, whereas B sorts an ordinal variable by value (8,6,3,5,4) with a redundant gradient, scrambling the relationship.
Nearly identical charts; B states the insight in a subtitle and uses short tidy leader lines, while A has a long diagonal leader crossing the data and unused headroom to 1.5 °C.
A's red median ticks and insight subtitle make the Gentoo gap pop, while B's grey medians nearly vanish among the points and its top median label collides with the frame.
B encodes the average with a distinct diamond shape and adds a spread column so the reader need not subtract, plus a headline subtitle, while A relies on colour alone and a footnote.
A's masked lower triangle drops the redundant half and the 1.00 diagonal with larger, readable cell labels, while B shows the full redundant matrix with small annotations.
Both share the y-axis; B places end-of-line values cleanly to the right and adds a legend and zero baseline, whereas A's end labels sit on top of the grey chick lines.
Essentially the same curves; B adds a headline subtitle and per-panel fold-range AUC notes, giving the reader more context than A's single footnote.
A's insight title, fit line and well-placed outlier callouts (Botswana, Qatar) tell a sharper story, though it omits the 9 FSU countries that B includes and B's long crossing Qatar leader is messier.
A's log scale keeps all five trajectories legible with direct labels, while B's linear axis crushes MSFT/AMZN/AAPL/IBM into a tangle at the bottom and duplicates labels with a legend.
Near-identical histograms; B's accent-red JFK flat-fare bar and context-rich title/subtitle make the notable feature pop slightly better than A's arrow.
Both correct (97% vs 14%); A is clean with a labelled y-axis, while B's dashed all-passenger line runs through the 37% label and its own text, and floating gap annotations add clutter.
